## Summary
"Amazon Technologies Inc." is the name on 208 IEEE blocks (the first, 28:EF:01, from January 2010; the latest updated 27 October 2026) registered to a P.O. Box in Reno, Nevada [1][2]; it is the entity under which Amazon's consumer hardware carries its addresses, so the parent is taken to be Amazon.com, Inc. on the strength of the registrant name and the Amazon-branded products involved [3][4], and no founding date for the subsidiary itself was found. A MAC in this block is an Amazon device: most likely an Echo smart speaker or display (announced November 2014, widely available mid-2015, dual-band 802.11a/b/g/n and Bluetooth A2DP/AVRCP at launch, with a Zigbee smart-home hub in Echo Plus and the 4th-generation Echo) [3], a Fire TV stick, box or Cube (802.11ac from the 2nd generation, 802.11ax on the 2nd-gen Cube and later sticks, Wi-Fi 6E on the 2022 Cube, Bluetooth up to 5.2, on Qualcomm, Broadcom, MediaTek MT8695/MT8696/MT8698 or Amlogic silicon) [5], a Fire tablet (MediaTek MT8163/MT8168, 802.11ac dual-band, Bluetooth 5.0 LE; the line was discontinued in 2026) [9] or a Kindle (dual-band Wi-Fi, Bluetooth for audio, NXP i.MX7D or MediaTek MT8113) [10]. Whether the Ring and eero subsidiaries use this registrant or their own blocks was not verified, so found_in is marked inferred for those lines; Ring Alarm Pro ships a 902-928 MHz radio [6], and eero mesh runs from Wi-Fi 5 (2016) through Wi-Fi 6, 6E and Wi-Fi 7 (Max 7, 2023) with Thread/Matter on recent models [7]. Expect more than Wi-Fi: Echo devices are Amazon Sidewalk bridges, speaking BLE plus 900 MHz LoRa and FSK, and Sidewalk is on by default without notifying the owner [4]. Security history is about data handling rather than radio exploits: the 2023 FTC settlement with Ring over employee video access and the December 2019 camera takeovers [6], and the 2018 misdirected-recordings and malicious-skill incidents on Alexa [8]. These are fixed-function devices and no randomization documentation was found, so that field is unknown; the FCC grantee code is left empty because the FCC ID mirrors returned 403.
